newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian employers soften tone on ERM parity rate.
newsitem.headline: Italian employers soften tone on ERM parity rate.

text.p: The leader of the Italian employers' federation Confindustria said the lira should return to the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) with a central parity of 1,050 per mark, but indicated a stronger level would be alright.
"The correct rate remains 1,050. But 1,010 would be acceptable if slightly forced," Giorgio Fossa said in an interview with newspaper Corriere della Sera on Sunday.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi said at the weekend negotiations to put the lira back into the ERM would start shortly.
Confindustria has repeatedly pressed for a central parity rate of around 1,050.

On the other hand, the French government, worried that Italian exporters have enjoyed too much of a competitive edge because of lira weakness in recent years, want the mark/lira central rate in the 900s.
The lira closed over the weekend at around the 1,006 level. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
